content:
[0] Love Mario Kart 64 and want to play it on your iPhone? You may have tried using Delta or another N64 emulator to make this wish come true. While emulators work, you can now run this classic racing game natively with Metal rendering on your iPhone.

[1] In today's video and article, we'll cover several key advantages of running Mario Kart 64 with native Metal rendering compared to running the same game via an emulator. Combined with Bluetooth controllers like the Mocagen MC1, this is the best way to play this Nintendo classic racing game on your iPhone.

[2] Native vs. Emulator?

[3] Libultraship is a library that re-implements the original N64 SDK on modern hardware. SpaghettiKart is a PC source code port of a decompiled original Mario Kart 64 cartridge that uses this library. Developer Chris Sotraidis has further repackaged SpaghettiCart into a native iPhone app called SpaghettiPad, providing native Metal rendering, Bluetooth controller support, enhanced visual effects, and more.

[4] Video Tutorial

[5] While it's more convenient to run Mario Kart 64 on iPhone using an emulator like Delta, running Mario Kart 64 natively on iPhone with SpaghettiPad offers a wider screen aspect ratio, frame rates up to 120 fps, higher resolution textures, overall better fps performance, plus some extra settings that emulators lack. Although SpaghettiPad isn't completely bug-free, I've experienced it firsthand and feel it has far fewer issues than the emulator.

[6] A good example is Luigi Raceway, which has a giant screen that displays your race progress. On the emulator version, the giant screen looks like it's running at a very low, choppy frame rate, but on the native version it runs stably at a much higher frame rate. I noticed many similar subtle examples during my playthrough.

[7] Disclaimer: I own an original Mario Kart 64 cartridge. If you also have a cartridge, you can dump the required ROM file yourself. We won't teach you how to dump or download any ROMs.

[8] How to Run Mario Kart 64 Natively on iPhone

[9] Install iLoader

[10] While iLoader can directly sideload .ipa files onto your iPhone, this tutorial mainly uses it to help install SideStore.

[11] Step One: Download iLoader from GitHub.

[12] Step Two: Mount iloader.dmg, then drag the iLoader application into the Applications folder.

[13] Step Three: Open iLoader, then connect your iPhone to your Mac using a USB cable. If a "Trust This Computer" prompt appears, select Trust and enter your device's passcode.

[14] Step Four: Click refresh under Devices, and you should see your iPhone appear in the list.

[15] Step Five: Enter your Apple ID email and password, then click Login. This Apple ID doesn't have to be tied to the account on your iPhone, nor does it need to be registered as an Apple developer. If you have two-factor authentication enabled, you'll need to enter the verification code received from Apple.

[16] Install SideStore

[17] SideStore is a fork of AltStore that can add software sources, install .ipa files, and automatically sign and re-sign apps in the background to avoid Apple's 7-day developer signing expiration. When SideStore is used together with LocalDevVPN, it enables truly wireless, Mac-free side载 app management.

[18] Every app installed with SideStore requires registering an App ID with Apple, and Apple limits non-developer logins to registering 10 App IDs per week. After one week, these App IDs will automatically expire.

[19] Apps installed using a SideStore account logged in as a non-developer can have a maximum of 3 active at any time, and SideStore itself counts as one of them.

[20] Each app's signature will expire after seven days, but you can manually re-sign at any time. However, when SideStore is connected to LocalDevVPN, it will automatically re-sign in the background and re-register App IDs for installed apps without needing a computer.

[21] Step Six: Open iLoader on the connected Mac, then in the Installers section select SideStore (Stable) to install it on your iPhone.

[22] Step Seven: On your iPhone, go to "Settings" → "General" → "VPN & Device Management", then tap the item under Developer App that says "Untrusted". On the next page tap "Trust" then "Allow".

[23] Step Eight: Open SideStore on your iPhone. For the network permission popup, you can select "Don't Allow", but for notification permissions, you should select "Allow".

[24] Install LocalDevVPN

[25] LocalDevVPN is a free App Store application that acts as a loopback VPN, creating a virtual interface that points back to your iPhone. It can trick iOS into thinking there's a paired Mac connected to your iPhone, thereby providing debugging tools for installing and re-signing side载 apps.

[26] Step Nine: On your iPhone, go to the App Store to install LocalDevVPN.

[27] Step Ten: Open LocalDevVPN, skip the welcome screen then tap "Connect" → "Allow". Enter your iPhone passcode to add the VPN configuration. LocalDevVPN's status should display "Connected".

[28] Install SpaghettiPad.ipa

[29] Step Eleven: On your iPhone, download SpaghettiPad.ipa from GitHub and save it to your iPhone's Downloads folder.

[30] Step Twelve: Open SideStore and tap the "My Apps" tab at the bottom.

[31] Step Thirteen: On the "My Apps" tab, tap the "+" button in the top-left corner, which will open the Files app interface. Select SpaghettiPad.ipa, and the system will prompt you to log into Apple ID on SideStore. You can use the same login name and password as iLoader.

[32] Step Fourteen: You should now see SpaghettiPad on your iPhone's home screen.

[33] Configure SpaghettiPad

[34] Step Fifteen: Through the Files app, move the Mario Kart 64 (USA).z64 ROM file to "On My iPhone" → "SpaghettiPad".

[35] Step Sixteen: Open SpaghettiPad on your iPhone, then tap "Rescan" on the "Add Game" popup. The next popup should display "Found Mario Kart 64 (US)". Tap "OK" to confirm. You'll see the screen go black for a while, then you'll see the "libultraship" startup screen, followed by the Mario Kart 64 title screen.

[36] Step Seventeen: Download the Mario Kart 64 HD texture pack and save the .o2r file to "On My iPhone" → "SpaghettiPad" → "mods".

[37] Step Eighteen: Open SpaghettiPad and tap the ellipsis button to open settings. Tap "Enhancements" → "Texture Pack" → "Re-check". You should see a popup saying "Texture Pack Detected". Tap "OK". Tap the power button in the top-right corner to exit SpaghettiPad, then relaunch SpaghettiPad to load the texture pack.

[38] Disable libultraship Startup Screen

[39] Step Nineteen: Open SpaghettiPad's settings again and tap "General". Under "Startup Behavior", select "Vanilla". From now on, when you reopen SpaghettiPad, it will skip the libultraship startup screen.

[40] Enable Higher Mario Kart 64 Frame Rate

[41] Step Twenty: Open SpaghettiPad's settings again and tap "Graphics". Tap "60 FPS" to jump straight to a 60 FPS frame rate. If your device supports ProMotion, you can even select 120 FPS.

[42] Connect Controller

[43] There are many USB and Bluetooth controller options for iPhone gaming, including Nintendo's own Switch Pro Controller, but the one I've been enjoying the most recently is this affordably priced Mocagen MC1. It's a slide-style controller that holds your iPhone inside and connects via Bluetooth. It features Hall effect analog sticks, USB-C charging, vibration, dual triggers, RGB lighting, and more. I tested it firsthand, and it works great with Mario Kart 64 on iPhone, plus the build quality is decent for the price.

[44] 9to5Mac's Take

[45] Emulating Mario Kart 64 using apps like Delta may be simpler, but installing SpaghettiPad on iPhone isn't that difficult either, and the experience is much better. SpaghettiPad provides a full-screen gaming experience, higher resolution textures, and significantly higher frame rates compared to the emulator version. If you're looking for the best way to play this classic game on the go, this is it.

[46] What do you think? Share your thoughts in the comments!
